Cross-cutting observation: WP-006 required 3 code-review cycles due to a recurring ES5 event-listener accumulation pattern on persistent DOM elements. The fix (module-level handler var + removeEventListener before re-wiring + removeEventListener in cleanup before nulling) is now established in config-stores.js and config.js. Future ES5 GUI modules registering listeners on persistent elements must adopt this pattern from the start — recommend codifying it in the GUI constraints document as a named convention.

outcome_summary: Delivered a full CRUD Stores tab for the MCP Server GUI Configuration screen, enabling users to view, add, import, edit, remove, reorder, and set the default store without CLI commands. The approach extended the backend with a new domain-split handler file (api-stores.ts), a hot-reload mechanism (reloadStoreContext()), and a 700-line ES5 frontend module (config-stores.js); the full regression suite of 3,944 tests passes with zero regressions. A notable result was the 3-cycle rework on WP-006 that uncovered an ES5 event-listener accumulation pattern on persistent DOM elements, establishing a removeEventListener lifecycle convention now documented in the codebase.
project_summary: This project adds a full CRUD Stores tab to the MCP Server GUI Configuration screen, enabling users to view, add, import, edit, remove, reorder, and set the default store without CLI commands. The backend is extended with write endpoints and a hot-reload mechanism that reinitializes the in-memory store context after configuration changes, so the running server reflects store mutations immediately without restart.
